correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the norm from its definition. Pairwise disjoint segments have distinct endpoints, giving the global upper constant \(\sqrt2\), and an adjacent sign-changing edge attains it. A recursive three-edge coloring partitions all edges into matchings. Each matching is an admissible family of one-edge segments, so \(N_1(x)^2\) is at least one third of the full edge energy. Summing \(2|ab|\le t|a|^2+t^{-1}|b|^2\) with \(t=1/\sqrt2\) yields \(E(x)\ge(3-2\sqrt2)\|x\|_2^2\); the root coefficient is larger. For a segment indicator, every nonzero variation uses a distinct support node and the branch-off construction realizes one such variation at every support node, proving equality.

value.rationale: The first-attempt norm is a motivated object singled out by the source as the natural dyadic-tree James-variation construction whose precise failure motivates the final space. The result gives a nontrivial quantitative upgrade: the displayed canonical distortion certificate drops from about \(9.35\) to at most about \(5.91\), the upper comparison constant is determined exactly, and the segment blow-up is made exact.
